selected_need: Transform tacit expert judgments into reproducible decision patterns and quality intent derivations
intended_user_or_segment: Organizations that rely on veteran reviewers, operators, managers, or specialists whose quality knowledge is mostly tacit
context_summary: Experts often cannot define quality abstractly, but they can judge concrete cases. The framework must extract reusable patterns from those judgments without treating expert opinion as self-justifying truth.
hypothesis: A case-based extraction and reproduction framework can make tacit quality knowledge executable by humans and AI while preserving context, exceptions, and loss boundaries.
rejected_alternatives: Collect generic know-how without concrete cases.
Promote inferred review-history patterns directly to active knowledge without validation.
explicit_risks: Patterns may overfit one expert or one department unless counterexamples, applicability boundaries, and multi-expert aggregation are explicit.
delivery_validation_requirements: Validate extracted patterns on unseen cases and require acceptable agreement by non-experts or AI agents.
need: Preserve tacit expert judgment as reusable organizational quality knowledge.
intent: Define entities, workflows, schemas, culture aggregation, and reproduction tests that turn case judgments into decision patterns and quality intent derivations.
context: QIF baseline exists; this framework adds the upstream extraction layer and must remain domain-general, non-surveillant, and governance-backed.
